requirements.statement: B0-6 / B4s, owner decisions 132/377: a reservation stranded by a service restart releases and settles exactly once, frees capacity, and writes no terminal or terminal-outbox row; the original B0-2 terminal test stays skipped.

Decision 382: every lifetime-cap registry entry has kind and nonempty ends; count, bytes and time bind an existing real past-limit test; validation, read_only and precondition require ends only. New/increased sites remain guarded; only six source-proven stale sites may be removed.
O0c / B0-6 P3: failed-before-launch lease lifecycles beyond the lease verification limit must leave live capacity counts readable after their real, exactly-once releases.

RS-8 / B0-6: lease, reservation, open-binding and result-custody settlement rows recover across pre-settlement stops, cuts before and after release, and lost post-commit replies, with stable replay and baseline live capacity.

RS-8 / B0-6: driver-entry and preparation memory rows retain custody for a live instance, recover across lost registration replies and cuts before and after recovery release, preserve replay after clock rollback, and permit unattended orchestration close.
RS-8: independently disabling each covered settlement or memory recovery release must make that same row fail its ordinary release oracle.

RS-8: actual unsent/expired/successor lease and companion custody releases, lease-to-reservation transfer, custody retention, normal memory retirement, refusal and handover paths, primary and unattended orchestration close, and authenticated denial release once and replay without changing their first register release.

O0c: real populations beyond reduced session directory, day, setup-project, rollout-read, fair-queue and SQLite cursor count limits demonstrate bounded work or refusal, with subsequent scanning/admission/read scopes usable.

O0c / decision 382: the session first-record parser accepts an exact MAX_FIRST_RECORD_BYTES JSON record and refuses one byte beyond the production limit, including when the excess and newline arrive in the next read block.
